summary: Both sides draw a slowly morphing, colour-cycling 2D lobed figure, but the original is a large upright bilaterally-symmetric butterfly on a 6.00 s cycle with a huge slow brightness envelope (long total blackouts, then a full-canvas bright regime), while the port is a small hollow diagonal lens/spindle on a 10.00 s cycle whose brightness never leaves a narrow band.
observations: Neither side exposes any controls: meta.json sides.orig.controls and sides.port.controls are both empty, and --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for both. Control surfaces match.
Both sides compile and animate with no compileError/runtimeError, over every window tested (6 s to 400 s) at 10/20/40 fps and seeds 1, 7 and 1234. Neither is black or frozen.

SHAPE (48x48 grid, t=0-4.3 s): original draws one large upright butterfly — broad swept wings above, a tapering body/tail below, feathery antenna specks — with soft filled magenta lobes covering ~50% of the grid (lit fraction 50-51% at t=0.15 s and 1.15 s). Port at the same moments draws a small NE-SW diagonal lens/spindle with a DARK HOLLOW CENTRE and thin coloured rim, lighting only 11-20% of the grid.

SYMMETRY (16x16 default rig, --dump, normalized left-right mirror difference sum|p-mirror(p)| / sum|p|): original is EXACTLY mirror-symmetric about the vertical axis for the first ~4 s — 0.00 at t=0.15 s, 0.00 at 1.85 s, 0.01 at 3.55 s — then loses it (1.40 at 5.25 s and 0.9-2.0 thereafter). The port is never mirror-symmetric: 1.20 at t=0.15 s, 1.65 at 1.85 s, 1.54 at 3.55 s, and 0.42-1.77 across a 40 s scan. The original's signature opening butterfly is absent from the port.

ORIENTATION / ELONGATION (48x48, intensity second moments over 60 one-second samples): original's figure is broad, aspect ratio (sqrt of eigenvalue ratio) 1.02-2.4 across the whole scan. The port's is a thin spindle, aspect ratio repeatedly 3.5-5.1 (t=3.15, 4.15, 5.15, 14.15, 22.15, 24.15, 46.15, 52.15, 56.15 s), and holds one fixed oblique angle for multi-second stretches (about -52 deg for t=0-3 s, +53 deg for t=4-8 s, +24 deg for t=9-11 s) before jumping.

MOTION RHYTHM (autocorrelation of raw meanBrightness and motionLit series from stats.json, no binning): the original's fundamental cycle is 120 frames at 20 fps = 6.00 s (peak 0.85 over t=0-40 s, 0.85 over t=170-240 s; harmonics at 12.00 s and 18.00 s). The port's is 200 frames at 20 fps = 10.00 s (peak 0.70 and 0.77 over the same two segments; harmonics at 5.00 s and 15.00 s). The port's morph cycle is ~1.67x too slow.

Both sides' base cycle is FRAME-RATE INVARIANT: the same lag scan gives the original 6.00 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps (60/120/240 frames) and the port 10.00 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps (100/200/399 frames). No frame-rate-coupling bug on either side's base cycle.

BRIGHTNESS ENVELOPE / REGIMES — the largest divergence. Over 400 s at 20 fps the original spends 28.0% of frames completely dark (meanBrightness < 0.5), in long contiguous gaps (roughly t=48-95 s and t=255-297 s), and reaches a full-canvas bright regime peaking at meanBrightness 26 (10 s bins average 20-22 around t=105-125 s and t=305-330 s). The port over the identical run never goes dark at all (0.0% of frames, min meanBrightness 1) and its 10 s bins stay inside 2.9-5.8 for the whole 400 s, max 17. The same holds at 10 fps over 400 s: original darkFrac 0.320, min 0, max 22; port darkFrac 0.000, min 1, max 19.

The original's regimes are visible directly at 48x48: t=50-94 s is entirely black, then from ~t=100 s a green veiny/cellular texture grows in and by t=113-120 s fills the whole 48x48 canvas. The port over that same 50-120 s window keeps producing the same small-to-medium lens and spindle figures with no dark gap and no canvas-filling regime. The whole-window rhythm images make this unmistakable: orig-rhythm over 400 s shows alternating coloured-streak / solid-black / solid-colour-block bands; port-rhythm over 400 s is one uniform dim texture end to end.

COLOUR: the original holds ONE saturated hue at a time and walks it slowly (magenta/pink through t~4.3 s, then teal/green from ~5.0 s, later yellow-olive and green regimes). Mean saturation of the per-frame mean RGB over 400 s is 0.913. The port paints many hues at once as thin rainbow fringes on its rim, so nothing dominates: its per-frame mean RGB is essentially neutral grey (avgR 4.34, avgG 4.29, avgB 4.27 over 400 s) and its frame-mean saturation is 0.203.

Both sides are RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT in the same way: re-rendering at --grid 16x16 and --grid 48x48 shows the same figure, just coarser or finer, with no change in feature count. No finding on this axis.
Both sides are SEED-INDEPENDENT: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce visually indistinguishable 60 s sheets on each side, so this is a deterministic pattern and the divergences above are not an RNG artefact.

Caveat about the original, not a port bug: while the original's 6.00 s base cycle is fps-invariant, its SLOW envelope schedule is not — the first sustained blackout starts at t=49.3 s at 20 fps, at t=1.9 s at 40 fps, and does not occur at all within 120 s at 10 fps. The original appears to carry a numerically chaotic slow accumulator. The robust, rate-independent fact is that the original's envelope swings between full black and a canvas-filling bright regime at every rate tested, and the port's does not swing at all.
feedback: The opening figure is wrong. The original's first ~4 s is a LARGE UPRIGHT BUTTERFLY that is exactly mirror-symmetric about the vertical centre axis (measured left-right mirror difference 0.00-0.01) — broad wings up top, tapering body below — filling ~50% of the grid with soft FILLED magenta lobes. The port draws a small OBLIQUE lens/spindle at roughly -52 deg with a hollow dark centre, lighting only 11-20% of the grid and never symmetric (0.42 at best, typically 1.2-1.7). Restore the upright, vertically-mirrored orientation and the filled interior; the current shape reads as a diagonal eye, not a butterfly.

The figure is too thin. The original's silhouette stays broad — aspect ratio 1.0-2.4 across a 60 s scan — while the port repeatedly stretches to aspect 3.5-5.1. Whatever is scaling the two axes is being driven far too hard in one direction.

The morph cycle is ~1.67x too slow: original's fundamental is 6.00 s (120 frames at 20 fps, confirmed by autocorrelation in two separate 40-70 s segments and at 10/20/40 fps), the port's is 10.00 s. Speeding the port's cycle by 5/3 should line the breathing rhythm up.

Colour is the second-biggest gap. The original shows ONE saturated hue over the whole figure at any instant and walks that hue slowly across the run (magenta -> teal -> yellow-olive -> green); its per-frame mean RGB has saturation 0.913. The port fringes every edge with several hues at once, so its per-frame mean RGB is neutral grey (R 4.34 / G 4.29 / B 4.27, saturation 0.203). Drive the whole figure from a single slowly-advancing hue rather than mapping hue to position/edge.

The port is missing the original's slow amplitude envelope entirely, and this is what a viewer watching all evening would notice most. Over 400 s the original goes COMPLETELY BLACK for 28-32% of frames in gaps tens of seconds long, and between gaps swells until a coloured veiny texture fills the entire canvas (mean brightness peaking at 22-26, 10 s bins averaging 20-22). The port never goes dark (0.0% of frames at both 10 and 20 fps) and never exceeds mean 17-19; its 10 s bins sit in 2.9-5.8 for the whole run. The port needs a slow drifting scale/brightness term that lets the figure both vanish for long stretches and grow past the canvas edge.

Do not chase per-frame alignment with the original's late-run regimes: the original's slow envelope schedule is fps-sensitive (first blackout at 49.3 s at 20 fps, 1.9 s at 40 fps, absent within 120 s at 10 fps). Match the CHARACTER — long total blackouts alternating with a canvas-filling bright regime — not the specific times.
